newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs higher in late Tokyo, led by cash buying.
newsitem.headline: JGBs higher in late Tokyo, led by cash buying.

text.p: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and futures were higher by late trade on Wednesday, supported by cash bond buying from local banks and brokers.
Widespread expectations that Japanese institutional investors may increase cash JGB buying from April provided underlining strength to the market, traders said.

There was also a view, they say, that some operators were eager to cover short positions in the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB. This resulted in the bond's yield falling to another record low of 2.290 percent soon after midday. The key bond yield stood at 2.300 percent at 0628 GMT.
The yield was 2.315 percent at Tuesday's finish.
Key June 10-year JGB futures contract closed at 125.75 on Wednesday, up from Tuesday's 125.53 finish.
The June moved within a range of 125.60 to 125.80 with a total 66,516 contracts changing hands.
"The recent rally in the benchmark 182nd issue was something unusual," said a senior dealer at city bank's securities unit.
Given a higher-than-usual repo rate ahead of the fiscal year-end, some operators were buying back the benchmark 182nd issue instead of borrowing the bond, traders said.
The collateralised repo rate for contracts beyond the end of March was at 0.50 percent, up by 10 basis points from a week ago, repo dealers said.
Traders also said short-covering demand for the 182nd issue was particularly strong from one local major broker.
The short positions held by the broker are the legacy of a previous attempt to hedge against large-lot purchases of municipal bonds from investors, they said.
Meanwhile, some investors were unloading part of their corporate bond holdings for JGBs. Such "flight-to-quality" demand also underscored the bullish tone, traders said.
But topside room was seen limited for now, traders said.

"The market hit a short-term ceiling today as people had considered certain levels as a target, such as 125.80 for the June contract, 2.30 percent for the 182nd issue and 2.50 percent for the March 193rd issue," the senior dealer said.

Yasunari Ueno, chief market economist at Fuji Securities, said that the JGB market may face a selling phase, albeit briefly, by the end of March. "The stock market is highly likely to be lifted up somehow by the end of March such as by a government announcement of concrete steps to raise land liquidity. If so, JGBs may be sold," he said.
"Investors said they are hesitant to hold JGBs if the yields are below 2.5 percent. That means the market's topside will soon be capped," said a senior economist at a long-term credit bank.
Many operators are focused on the outcome of a probe by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) into scandal-hit Nomura Securities Co Ltd, traders said.

The Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo) and the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday they would wait for SESC's results before deciding whether to suspend their bond business with Nomura. -- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
